text:
The Rangers' goaltending has been a story all autumn, from James Reimer's contract being terminated after he cleared waivers to Dylan Garand carrying the load. On Wednesday in Calgary, Joonas Korpisalo, back after a long stint on injured reserve, made it a quieter story for a night: 29 saves on 30 shots in a 3-1 win.

The first 20 minutes went nowhere, 0.74 expected goals (the quality of chances) for New York to 0.82 for Calgary, and Korpisalo's stop on a 19% Matvei Gridin look was the best chance of the period. Mika Zibanejad broke it open 59 seconds into the second with a wrist shot that had about a 4% chance of going in, then added a power-play slap shot at 10:52. Alexis Lafrenière assisted on both. The first goal took New York from 48% to 66% to win; the second pushed it to 87%.

Calgary got one back on the power play 7:41 into the third, Adam Klapka finishing a 26% chance from Ryan Strome and Yegor Sharangovich. Klapka, never drafted and a graduate of the Calgary Wranglers, has made a habit of being in the right place. Korpisalo's save on Mikael Backlund later in the third was the stop that mattered most, and Tye Kartye sealed it with seven seconds left, finishing a 66% chance set up by J.T. Miller.

At even strength the Flames were slightly better, 1.61 expected goals to 1.45, and they deserved to win 55% of replays by our count. New York's edge came from a heavy third period (1.80 expected goals to 0.83) and from Zibanejad finishing two low-percentage looks. Devin Cooley, back in Calgary's net, was fine, 21 of 23. The Flames played without Kevin Bahl, whose season-ending injury has dominated the headlines around the team and tested its defensive depth.

For the Rangers, a road win with the starting goalie looking like himself is worth more than the two points. Kartye, who has been playing on J.T. Miller's line, keeps giving the Rangers reasons to call him a building block.
headline: Korpisalo steadies the Rangers in Calgary
